subject: botany_2
question_text: Given the coding strand of DNA in a transcription unit as 5'-AATGCAGCTATTAGG-3', write the sequence of (a) its complementary strand (b) the mRNA.

verification.note: Sourced from "Sr. Botany — My Baby Bullet-Q" (Sri Publishers, STAR-Q Pass Track), book p.43, printed question 94. Botany-II holds only ONE source book: the TSBIE Basic Learning Material in hand covers physics only, and no Telangana Botany-II board paper is in the corpus, so the two-book union check and the board back-test are BOTH structurally impossible for this card — "not checked" does NOT mean "checked and clean". Run both the moment a second source or a real paper arrives. The mark split is a claim until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it. BOOK ERROR, corrected on this card. The guide answers (b) with 3'-UUACGUCGAUAAUCC-5', which is simply part (a) with U for T — that is the TEMPLATE strand, not the message. The mRNA has the SAME sequence as the CODING strand, with uracil in place of thymine: 5'-AAUGCAGCUAUUAGG-3'. Part (a) as printed is correct.

insider_note: Part (b) is the trap and the guide falls into it. The mRNA copies the CODING strand, not the template. Write the coding strand out and change every T to U.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: The complementary strand
steps.margin_note: Write both strands with their 5' and 3' ends marked. The direction is part of the mark.
lines: 5'-A A T G C A G C T A T T A G G-3'
Pair A with T and G with C, and run the answer
3'-T T A C G T C G A T A A T C C-5'
steps.why: The two strands are antiparallel, so the complement is written 3' to 5' when the coding strand is written 5' to 3'.
common_mistakes: Writing the complement 5' to 3'. The two strands run in OPPOSITE directions.
Pairing A with G. A pairs with T, and G pairs with C.
steps.memory_tip: Swap each base for its partner, and flip the direction.

steps.label: The mRNA
steps.margin_note: Write the answer and then the one-line rule. That rule is what stops the mistake recurring.

lines.text: The mRNA copies the CODING strand, with U

lines: 5'-A A U G C A G C U A U U A G G-3'
It is the coding strand with every T replaced
It is NOT the complementary strand with U.
steps.why: RNA polymerase reads the TEMPLATE strand, so what it builds comes out matching the OTHER strand — the coding strand — which is why that strand is called coding at all.
common_mistakes: Giving the template strand with U instead of T. That is the guide's printed answer and it is wrong.
Writing the mRNA 3' to 5'. The mRNA runs 5' to 3', like the coding strand.
steps.memory_tip: Coding strand, T becomes U, direction unchanged.
